speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Can you tell me how long these skin lesions have been present and have they changed in appearance since they first appeared?

speaker: Patient
text: 2-year-old female. The patient's mother reports noticing multiple painless, nonpruritic papules on the child's abdomen. The child attends daycare where another child was reported to have similar lesions recently. Patient's brother had chickenpox one month ago. Immunizations are up-to-date.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the brother's recent chickenpox and the daycare exposure, I need to clarify if the lesions are fluid-filled vesicles or solid papules, and if they appeared in crops or all at once. Are there any lesions on the face or scalp?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Skin-colored, nontender, pearly papules with central umbilication on the abdomen and extremities.

speaker: Doctor
text: The description of pearly, umbilicated papules is classic for Molluscum contagiosum. Do you have any lesions in the genital or perianal area, and has the child attempted to scratch or pick at them?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Previously healthy, up-to-date immunizations, no significant illnesses. Social history: Attends daycare three times per week.

speaker: Doctor
text: The clinical presentation of skin-colored, pearly, umbilicated papules in a healthy 2-year-old with daycare exposure is pathognomonic for Molluscum contagiosum, so no further testing is required. DIAGNOSIS READY: Molluscum contagiosum
